summary: For strix's local "brain," the strongest 2025-2026 picks are the Qwen3 family (Apache-2.0, best-in-class open tool-calling and native MCP support) and Mistral's Apache-2.0 models (Small 3.1/3.2 24B and the agent-tuned Devstral). On the Berkeley Function Calling Leaderboard, Llama 3.1 Instruct (405B/70B/8B) actually posts the highest raw FC AST scores among open models, but its custom license carries an Acceptable Use Policy that restricts "espionage," weapons/critical-infrastructure work, and a 700M-MAU competitor clause — a real liability for an offensive-security product you intend to ship commercially. Apache-2.0 models (Qwen3, Mistral/Mixtral, DeepSeek-R1 distills derived from Qwen) give you clean commercial freedom with no API and full offline operation. The practical default is Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507 (MoE, ~3B active, ~21GB at Q4 — fast and agentic on a 24GB GPU/32GB unified), with Qwen3-8B/14B for 16GB and Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507 for 8GB tiers; all expose tool calls via `<tool_call>` JSON and switch thinking on/off. A key independent finding (TrustedSec self-hosted offensive-security benchmark) is that agent-tuned mid-size models (Devstral) beat larger ones on tool-use efficiency and latency, while ALL local models hit a wall on multi-step exploit chaining — so strix should lean on its deterministic Scope Guard + explicit planning scaffolds rather than expecting the model to reason an entire kill-chain unaided. Pure reasoning models (DeepSeek-R1 distills, QwQ) reason well but historically emit broken/empty tool_calls, so keep them as optional "planner/advisor" backends, not the tool-executing loop.

recommendations.name: Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507 (DEFAULT for 24GB GPU / 32GB+ unified)
recommendations.why: Best overall fit: MoE with only ~3B active params, so it runs fast (~tps of a small model) while reasoning like a much larger one. Leading open tool-calling, native MCP support, reliable <tool_call> JSON, 256K context (262,144 native) for long ROE/scope docs and audit history. 2507 update specifically improved tool usage and agentic behavior. Tradeoffs: MoE needs the whole model resident (~21GB Q4_K_M); for tight VRAM, offload experts to RAM (works at ~30 tps even on small GPUs with enough system RAM).
recommendations.integration: HTTP/RPC — keep the existing Ollama backend (`ollama run qwen3:30b-a3b-instruct-2507` or unsloth GGUF via llama.cpp server); strix already calls Ollama. Parse the <tool_call> JSON into the plugin registry.
recommendations.maturity: Very active; Alibaba flagship open series, huge community, first-class llama.cpp/Ollama/Unsloth support

recommendations.name: Qwen3-8B / Qwen3-14B (16GB tier)
recommendations.why: Sweet spot for a 16GB GPU (e.g., 4060 Ti 16GB / 4070 Ti Super) or 16GB Mac. Same Apache-2.0 license, same <tool_call> format, thinking-mode toggle, 128K context. 14B at Q4_K_M ~9GB leaves room for context; 8B ~5GB is comfortable with long context. Strong enough for plan->guard->execute loops; step down to 8B if you need bigger context windows or vision side-tools.

recommendations.name: Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507 (8GB tier / laptop / air-gapped minimal)
recommendations.why: Smallest model that is genuinely usable for agentic tool calling — documented driving real agents via llama.cpp at Q8. ~3-5GB at Q4-Q8, fits an 8GB GPU or even CPU/iGPU with 16GB RAM. Ideal for the user's stripped terminal-only Lenovo dev machine. Expect more supervision and tighter prompting; pair with strix's Scope Guard and structured plan schema to compensate for weaker long-horizon reasoning.
recommendations.integration: HTTP/RPC via Ollama/llama.cpp; also embeddable through llama.cpp server on CPU

recommendations.name: Mistral-Small-3.2-24B-Instruct-2506 (alt default, 24GB tier)
recommendations.why: Apache-2.0, native function calling + JSON output, 128K context, knowledge-dense, runs on a single 24GB GPU or 32GB Mac at Q4 (~14-15GB). Strong instruction-following and a different model lineage than Qwen — valuable as a cross-check/fallback so strix isn't single-vendor. 3.2 fixed repetition/instruction issues over 3.1. Slightly behind Qwen3 on the very latest agent benchmarks but very stable.
recommendations.integration: HTTP/RPC via Ollama/llama.cpp; supports Mistral's tool-call schema
recommendations.maturity: Active; Mistral's mainline small model, well supported

recommendations.name: Devstral Small (Mistral, agent/tool-use specialist)
recommendations.why: Independent offensive-security benchmark (TrustedSec) found the Devstral family had the best tool-use EFFICIENCY: fewest turns per task (~1.7), lowest latency (~23s), 77% first-attempt solves — beating much larger models. Built for agent loops (SWE-style), so it's a natural fit for strix's execute engine where turn count and latency matter. Apache-2.0. Tradeoff: tuned for software-agent tasks; validate on your pentest tool schemas.
recommendations.maturity: Active Mistral release line for coding/agents

recommendations.name: DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-14B / 32B (optional PLANNER/advisor, not executor)
recommendations.why: Excellent step-by-step reasoning for engagement planning and analyzing findings; Qwen2.5-based distills are Apache-2.0. Use as a separate 'reasoning' backend that drafts the plan, which strix then converts to tool calls executed by Qwen3/Devstral. Hard tradeoff: distilled R1 variants are documented to emit empty/broken tool_calls — do NOT put them in the direct tool-calling loop. 14B ~9GB Q4, 32B ~20GB Q4.
recommendations.integration: HTTP/RPC via Ollama; strix uses it as a planning oracle, parses prose/JSON plan, then dispatches tools with a different model
recommendations.maturity: Popular (Jan 2025); note original R1-distill lacked FC, later R1-0528 added it

recommendations.name: Hermes 3 (Llama 3.1 8B/70B, Nous) — situational fallback
recommendations.why: Neutrally-aligned, steerable, with explicit structured-output and function-calling training and a built-in JSON-schema system prompt; far less 'twitchy' than base Llama-instruct when discussing exploit/memory-corruption topics — useful for the security-reasoning, no-refusal requirement. Tradeoff: inherits the Llama 3 community license + Acceptable Use Policy (700M-MAU cap, restricted-use carve-outs), so it is NOT a clean commercial base for a shipped offensive-security product. Keep as an operator-local option, not the bundled default.
recommendations.integration: HTTP/RPC via Ollama/llama.cpp; uses Hermes <tool_call> XML/JSON convention

pitfalls: LICENSE TRAP for an offensive-security product: Llama 3.x/4 are NOT Apache/OSI-open. Their custom license adds a 700M-MAU commercial cap, a competitor-product restriction, a ban on using outputs to train non-Llama models, and an Acceptable Use Policy that prohibits 'espionage,' weapons, and critical-infrastructure activities — directly adjacent to pentest use. Default to Apache-2.0 models (Qwen3, Mistral/Mixtral/Devstral, Qwen2.5-derived DeepSeek distills) for anything you ship.

ACCEPTABLE-USE / SAFETY-ALIGNMENT TRAP: Even Apache-2.0 models ship with usage policies and safety tuning. Gemma's terms incorporate Google's Prohibited Use Policy (attacks on critical infrastructure, etc.); Qwen/Gemma instruct models can refuse or hedge on offensive payloads. The Apache license governs the WEIGHTS (you're free), but the model's TRAINED REFUSALS still bite at runtime — budget for prompt engineering, role/scope framing, or operator-supplied uncensored variants (Dolphin/Hermes/abliterated) for legitimate authorized testing.

BFCL scores mislead for local use: Llama 3.1 405B/70B top the open BFCL AST rankings, but those sizes are not consumer-hardware-runnable, and high AST score != good multi-turn agentic behavior. Use BFCL multi-turn/agentic tracks and real task benchmarks, not single-call AST, to pick a model for strix's loop.

Reasoning models break tool calling: DeepSeek-R1 distills and QwQ reason well but are documented to return empty/malformed tool_calls; original R1 lacked function calling entirely. Don't wire a pure-reasoning model into the execute loop — use it only as a planner and have a tool-capable model dispatch.

Multi-step exploitation is a hard ceiling for ALL local models: the TrustedSec self-hosted benchmark found models know payload classes but fail to chain them (e.g., 0% on extraction-based SQLi). strix must NOT rely on the model to autonomously reason an end-to-end kill chain; provide explicit planning scaffolds, tool affordances, and let the deterministic Scope Guard + structured plan schema constrain and guide it.

MoE memory math: Qwen3-30B-A3B is fast (3B active) but still needs the FULL ~21GB (Q4) resident or expert-offloaded to RAM. Don't size VRAM by active params. For 8/16GB tiers, plan expert offload (needs 32-64GB system RAM) or drop to dense 4B/8B/14B.

Web-search noise / model hallucination: several 2026 'sources' reference unverifiable future models (Qwen3.5/3.6, Mistral Small 4, Gemma 4, Devstral-2, Claude-Opus-4-x). Pin strix's defaults to verifiable, downloadable 2025 releases (Qwen3-2507, Mistral-Small-3.2-2506, R1 distills) and re-validate model IDs against Hugging Face/Ollama before bundling.

Don't hardcode one tool-call dialect: Qwen/Hermes use <tool_call> JSON, Mistral uses its own schema, Llama uses yet another. Abstract the parser in strix's planner so you can swap backends without rewriting the engine; let Ollama's native tools API normalize where possible.
open_questions: What is strix's minimum target hardware? The default model choice differs sharply between an 8GB laptop (Qwen3-4B), a 16GB GPU (Qwen3-8B/14B), and a 24GB/Mac-32GB box (Qwen3-30B-A3B / Mistral-Small-3.2). Confirm the floor spec to pick THE default.

Will strix bundle/ship a model with the product, or only orchestrate whatever the operator pulls via Ollama? If bundling, Apache-2.0 (Qwen3/Mistral) is effectively mandatory; if operator-supplied, you can support Llama/Hermes/uncensored variants as opt-in.

How should refusals be handled for authorized testing? Decide policy: rely on prompt/scope framing with stock instruct models, support operator-loaded uncensored/abliterated models, or fine-tune. This is a product+legal decision, not purely technical.

Single model for plan+execute, or split planner (reasoning model) vs executor (tool-calling model)? A two-model design (R1-distill/QwQ planner -> Qwen3/Devstral executor) improves reasoning but doubles memory and complexity.

Should strix standardize on Ollama (simple, already integrated) or also support a raw llama.cpp server / embedded llama.cpp for true single-static-binary air-gapped distribution? Ollama is a separate dependency; embedding llama.cpp gets closer to the single-binary vision but is more work.
Vision needs? Mistral-Small-3.1/3.2 and some Qwen models are multimodal — if strix wants to read screenshots/diagrams of scope or web UIs, that narrows the model list.
